summary.title: NodeSchool
summary.one_liner: NodeSchool offers free, self-guided command-line lesson modules ("workshoppers") that teach Node.js, JavaScript and related topics, each installed via npm.
takeaways: Workshoppers are open source, self-guided lesson modules that mostly work offline.
Each workshopper is installed globally with npm and launched by typing its name in the terminal.
You need Node.js and a text editor to get started.
The catalogue covers core topics (JavaScript basics, streams, Markdown) and electives (functional JS, promises, ES6, Koa, React, CouchDB, shaders, and more).
summary.summary: The NodeSchool page is a catalogue of workshoppers, open source lesson modules for learning Node.js and related technologies. Lessons are self-guided, do not require attending a workshop, and mostly run offline. The page lists core workshoppers (such as javascripting, stream-adventure, and how-to-markdown) and electives on topics like functional JavaScript, promises, ES6, Koa, React, and CouchDB, each with its npm install command. Setup requires Node.js and a text editor.
